svg.title: Physical storage and address microscope — window_ffn_projection_input_view_c512_fp16
svg.desc: Physical allocations, exact byte counts, a worked producer/consumer address, lane words, and bank mapping specialized to this kernel. Native panel bank rows show address regions rather than hardware transaction cycles.
svg.text: 4 warps · Half operand elements (2 B) · 12,312 explicitly declared shared bytes
CTA-local storage actually used by this entry
Each cell = uint4 (16 B); each row = one native panel, 32 lane packets.
Barriers: +12,288 B, 3 × 8 B. Complete the copy before A loads.
Follow one address into lane 13 — bases and address spaces stay separate
First native M16×K16 A panel: lane 13 packet begins at +13×16 = +208 B.
Word 0 carries Half channels [2,3] for physical token row 3.
For staged A, add the selected slot and panel bases; for a direct load, add the global panel base.
Weights / B have a different map: selected B scalar is owned by lane 9, not lane 13.
Labels are panel-relative; add the model channel base. This is an operand fragment, not a contiguous token vector.
Address bits, banks, and the next consumer
mod 32. Lane 13 word 0 → bank 20. Cells read
Panel bases are 512-byte aligned. No extra XOR swizzle is present. Transaction splitting determines conflicts.
Shared reuse requires the source barrier sequence; register publication can stay inside the current warp.
The source determines cache policy. No cache residency, issue-cycle schedule, spill count or speedup is assumed.
